_note: Deut 28 with Lev 26 (the two sanction chapters). Seed drafted 2026-11-12 from the verses; every strength is a PROPOSAL for Lane (3 shared words, 2 same beat, 1 thematic). Spans are English numbering. Here = Deuteronomy, other = Leviticus.

sources.cite: Builder's reading of Deut 28 and Lev 26 in the Hebrew text (OSHB), compared verse by verse; shared lemma ids were checked by script.
sources.what: Pairs and strengths are proposals; Lane decides which to keep and at what strength.
sources.boundary_note: Tigay's Excursus 26 (the blessing and curse structure, Deut 28) is only a pointer to where the lists run: blessings 28:1–14, curses 28:15–68.

pairs.title: If you keep the commandments, blessings
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Both open the blessings with keeping and doing the commandments.

pairs.title: Rain in its season
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Same promise (rain given in its season); the word for rain differs, so only 'give' and 'season' are shared.

pairs.title: Enemies fall before you
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Same beat: enemies are beaten before Israel; the verbs differ (struck vs fall by the sword).

pairs.title: The LORD establishes you
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Same beat: God confirms Israel (a holy people / his covenant); one shared verb, 'establish'.

pairs.title: The yoke: broken, then iron
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Both name a yoke; Lev says God broke its bars, Deut says he puts an iron one on.

pairs.title: Egypt and slavery reversed
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Lev 26:13 brought you out of Egypt so you would not be slaves; Deut 28:68 sends you back to be sold as slaves.

pairs.title: But if you will not listen
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Both open the curses with not listening and not doing the commandments and statutes.

pairs.title: Consumption and fever
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): The same two disease words appear in both lists.

pairs.title: Seed sown, others consume it
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Same beat (sown seed lost); only 'seed' is shared and the eater differs (locust vs enemies).

pairs.title: Struck before your enemies, you flee
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Near word for word: struck before the enemy, and flee (Deut: seven ways; Lev: with none pursuing).

pairs.title: Sky and earth as metal
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Same image; the metals are swapped (Lev sky iron, soil bronze; Deut sky bronze, earth iron).
pairs.note: Tigay points to an Assyrian parallel to this image (figures-tigay item 20); not used here.

pairs.title: Pestilence
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): The same word for pestilence; in Lev it comes with the covenant sword, in Deut it clings until Israel is consumed.

pairs.title: Eating the flesh of sons and daughters
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Same four words: eat, flesh, sons, daughters. Deut adds the siege and the detail of 28:54–57.

pairs.title: Scattered among the nations
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Same beat (scattering); Deut says 'peoples', Lev 'nations' (the shared word, 'nations', turns up in Deut 28:65).
pairs.note: Only 'land' is shared inside these two verses, so no shared entry.

pairs.title: A fearful heart among the enemy
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Same beat: terror of heart in exile; Lev adds flight at a leaf's sound, Deut adds no rest and day-and-night dread. Could be a 3 on the shared 'heart'.

pairs.title: Animals
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Thematic only: in Lev wild animals rob you of children; in Deut animals eat the corpses.

pairs.title: Astonishment
pairs.strength_why: PROPOSED (builder): Thematic only: in Lev your enemies are astonished at the land; in Deut Israel becomes an astonishment among the peoples.
